title: Geophysical Characteristics of Low-Sulfide Epithermal Gold Mineralized Bodies —an Case Study of the Alinghe Mining Area on the South Bank of the Heilong River in China
content: The inability of geophysical methods to directly detect gold ore bodies remains a hot topic in the realm of gold geophysical exploration. Through the analysis of high-precision magnetic method, resistivity and induced polarization methods with the gradient arrays, electrical resistance tomography , and well logging, combined with the discovery of gold mineralization in exploration trenches and boreholes, it has been found that gold mineralization in the andesite distributed area can be classified into two types: terminal and channel. The terminal-type gold mineralization is marked by a buried depth of less than 30m, accompanied by varying degrees of silicification and pyritization. In contrast, the channel-type of gold mineralization is buried deeper than 30m and occurs within structural fractures or volcanic breccia mineralized alteration zones. The resistivity difference constitutes a significant geophysical indicator differentiating these two types of gold mineralization. Both types of gold mineralization are located adjacent to high-polarization anomaly areas, potentially suggesting characteristics of low-sulfur gold mineralization. These research results provide geophysical technical support for breakthroughs in the exploration of low-sulfide epithermal gold deposits and represent a valuable exploration in the field of directly detecting such gold deposits using geophysical methods.
